manage_providers.title: Manage providers
manage_providers.description: Add, edit and remove the AI providers and their API keys.

apply_proposals.title: Apply proposals

services.use.title: Use AI from other features
services.use.description: Other features may call the assistant on your behalf.

use.title: Run commands on hosts with the AI assistant
use.description: Let the assistant run any shell command on the hosts you select. Admins only by default.

view_all.title: View everyone's AI usage
view_all.description: See the tokens every user's AI calls used, not only your own. Admins only by default.

view.title: View the asset inventory
view.description: See the collected hosts, guests, containers, zones and connections. Admins only by default.

providers.label: Providers
providers.description: The AI services the assistant and agents can use.

globallyEnabled.label: AI assistant
globallyEnabled.description: Let users turn on the AI assistant. While this is off, the assistant is hidden and blocked for everyone.

privateEndpoints.label: Allowed private AI hosts
privateEndpoints.description: Hosts on your private network that users may point a provider at, such as a self-hosted Ollama. Put one host on each line.

opsConcurrency.label: AI assistant parallel hosts
opsConcurrency.description: How many hosts an assistant command runs on at the same time.

opsCommandTimeout.label: AI assistant command timeout (seconds)
opsCommandTimeout.description: How long a command may run on a host before it is stopped. The assistant can ask for up to 600.

opsOutputLimit.label: AI assistant output per host (characters)
opsOutputLimit.description: How much of each host's output is kept. Longer output keeps its start and end.

autoOpsPaused.label: Pause AI auto-ops
autoOpsPaused.description: Stops every AI task and approved plan that is running and refuses new ones, until turned off again.

autoOpsRunsPerHour.label: AI tasks per automation per hour
autoOpsRunsPerHour.description: More triggers in the same hour are skipped.

autoOpsRunTokens.label: Token budget per AI task
autoOpsRunTokens.description: A task that uses this many tokens is stopped and reports what it found.

autoOpsDailyTokens.label: Daily AI token budget per user
autoOpsDailyTokens.description: Once a user has used this many tokens today (UTC), their AI tasks are skipped or stopped.

assetsDailyCollect.label: Collect the asset inventory daily
assetsDailyCollect.description: Reads every host the collector can connect to once a day with one read-only script.

assetsAnnotateAfterCollect.label: Annotate assets after each collection
assetsAnnotateAfterCollect.description: A model writes each changed asset's role, importance and business system, and the dependencies the facts show.

assetsAnnotateRunTokens.label: Token budget per asset annotation run
assetsAnnotateRunTokens.description: A run stops once its model calls have used this many tokens; what it wrote stays.

exposureRetentionDays.label: Exposure history retention (days)
exposureRetentionDays.description: Keeps pending notices and evidence referenced by current entries regardless of age.

enableAiAssistant.label: Enable AI Assistant
enableAiAssistant.description: Allow the AI assistant to help in this host's terminal. Off by default, and still needs AI enabled for your account.

showPanel.label: Panel beside the terminal
showPanel.description: Offer a assistant panel next to this host's SSH terminal.

companionAutoOpen.label: Open the assistant panel with a terminal
companionAutoOpen.description: Show the assistant panel when a terminal opens on a host that has it.

companionSide.label: Assistant panel side
companionSide.description: Where the panel sits next to the terminal.

companionSize.label: Assistant panel size
companionSize.description: Width, or height at the bottom, in pixels.

companionEdgeButton.label: Assistant panel edge button
companionEdgeButton.description: Show a small button on the terminal edge to open the panel.

agents.title: AI Agent
agents.permissionDescription: Start coding agents on SSH hosts using configured AI providers. Agents can execute commands and change files as the SSH user.
agents.description: Run an agent in a directory on this host using a Termix AI provider.
agents.requirements: The host needs Node.js 22.19+ and the selected agent installed. SSH remote loopback forwarding must be allowed. Existing agent configurations are not overwritten.
agents.responsesRequired: Codex requires a Responses API endpoint. A Chat Completions-only endpoint cannot run Codex.
agents.piPermissions: Pi tools run with this SSH account’s permissions. Only launch in a directory you authorize the agent to modify.
agents.prompt: Ask the agent to work in this directory…
agents.noSessions: No agent sessions for this host.
agents.streamFailed: Agent stream disconnected. Reopen the session to reconnect.
agents.installSource: Official sources only: nodejs.org (SHA-256 verified) and registry.npmjs.org (locked package integrity). Installs for the SSH user in ~/.local/share/termix-agent-runtime; requires curl, tar, and Linux/macOS x64 or arm64. Does not change SSH forwarding policy.
agents.installSucceeded: Installation verified. You can now start the agent; SSH loopback remote forwarding must also be allowed.
agents.installFailed: Installation failed. Review the log and retry.
agents.forwardingScope: Linux with systemd/OpenSSH; requires root or passwordless sudo. Backs up and validates SSH configuration, then reloads it. Only the current SSH account and observed connection source receive loopback remote forwarding; existing local forwarding is preserved. Failed changes are rolled back.
agents.forwardingSucceeded: SSH loopback remote forwarding is ready. Start or resume the agent to open a new SSH connection.
agents.forwardingFailed: SSH forwarding configuration failed. Review the log; no unvalidated configuration is kept.
agents.attach: Attach a file from the host
agents.worktreeHint: Creates a new branch from HEAD. Uncommitted changes stay in the current directory. Existing worktrees are never deleted automatically.
agents.unavailable: Session is no longer accessible. Check your permissions or sign in again.
agents.shortcuts: Enter sends or queues · Shift+Enter adds a line · Esc interrupts and pauses the queue
agents.emptyTranscript: Send a message to get the agent started.

autoOps.intro: Auto-ops lets the assistant check your hosts on its own. An automation starts it on a schedule or when something goes wrong, and it writes a report or proposes a fix for you to approve. Start with a preset.

daily-patrol.title: Daily patrol
daily-patrol.description: Every morning at 09:00, checks every host's disks, memory, load, failed services, containers, certificates, updates, pending reboots and time sync, and reports by severity.

disk-cleanup.title: Disk space cleanup
disk-cleanup.description: When a disk stays at 85% or more for 5 minutes, finds what fills it and proposes a safe cleanup for you to approve. Business data is never touched.

host-down-triage.title: Host down triage
host-down-triage.description: When a host goes offline, probes it from other hosts and Proxmox, and reports whether it is the network, a stopped machine or SSH.

service-failure.title: Service failure
service-failure.description: When a health check starts failing, finds the systemd unit behind it, reads its status and log, and proposes a single restart for you to approve when that can help. Configuration is never changed.

container-anomaly.title: Container anomaly
container-anomaly.description: When a container exits, turns unhealthy or keeps restarting, reads its state, exit code, logs and memory, and proposes starting or restarting it once for you to approve. Nothing is removed.

resource-overload-cpu.title: CPU overload
resource-overload-cpu.description: When CPU stays at 95% or more for 15 minutes, finds the processes, services and containers behind it and reports what to do. Nothing is changed.

resource-overload-memory.title: Memory overload
resource-overload-memory.description: When memory stays at 95% or more for 10 minutes, finds what uses it, swapping and out-of-memory kills, and reports what to do. Nothing is changed.

security-updates-weekly.title: Weekly security updates
security-updates-weekly.description: Every Monday at 09:30, lists pending security updates by severity, pending reboots and the packages behind them, running and installed kernels and days since the last update, in one table for all hosts.

cert-expiry-weekly.title: Weekly certificate expiry
cert-expiry-weekly.description: Every Monday at 09:45, reads the expiry of Let's Encrypt, web server and Kubernetes certificates on every host and flags those under 30 days, critical under 7.
